On November 30, 2020, SushiSwap was exploited on Ethereum Mainnet due to improper access control around its Sushibar fee-reward logic. An attacker was able to withdraw protocol fees, resulting in approximately $15,000 in losses, which were later covered by the SushiSwap treasury. No user funds or pool liquidity were lost and the exploit was patched within hours. Lax access control in the Sushibar fee-rewards logic allowed an attacker to withdraw protocol fees by invoking reward-handling functions in an unintended sequence or manner not properly restricted to authorized actors.
